summary: This is a JUnit test class for the Thermostat class. It contains one focused test per possible outcome \u2014 heating, idle, and cooling in normal mode, the same three in eco mode, and one for the display string \u2014 so that a failure tells you exactly which behaviour broke.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is what marks a method as a test for the test runner to find and execute.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), keeping each test line short and readable.
The test name reads like a sentence describing the rule being checked, so a failure report names the broken behaviour without you having to open the code.
Each test builds its own thermostat with exactly the temperature it cares about, and false means eco mode is off. Fresh objects keep tests independent of one another.
Compares the expected value (first argument) with the actual result (second argument); if they differ, JUnit fails the test and shows both.
72 sits comfortably between the heating and cooling thresholds, so it exercises the middle branch rather than an edge.
Eco mode gets its own set of tests because switching the flag to true changes the thresholds, and each mode deserves separate coverage.
At 64 degrees a normal thermostat would still call for heat, but eco mode tolerates cooler air \u2014 this value is chosen to land just inside the eco heating range.
79 degrees is warm enough to trigger cooling even with eco mode's raised threshold, confirming the upper limit still works.
This last test checks the formatting method rather than the decision logic, verifying that the status is wrapped in the expected display text.
